newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-VOGTS CALLS UP DUNDEE FOR ALBANIA GAME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VOGTS CALLS UP DUNDEE FOR ALBANIA GAME.

text.p: South African-born Sean Dundee was added to the Germany squad on Monday by national coach Bertie Vogts for the group nine World Cup qualifier against Albania on Wednesday.
Vogts drafted in the uncapped Karlsruhe striker after Bayern Munich midfielder Mario Basler pulled out, with the coach's permission, because his girlfriend was due to give birth in the next few days.
Dundee, who was granted German citizenship at the end of last year, was due to travel with the squad anyway as an observer, to get to know the national team set-up.

The 24-year old striker, who will probably begin Wednesday's game on the bench, was due to make his Germany debut in a friendly against Israel in February but had to withdraw because of a calf injury.
"The last time I was unlucky. This time I've had a bit of luck," Dundee commented.
The match will take place in the Spanish city of Granada instead of Tirana, the original venue, because of concern about political unrest in Albania.
